title: One generation of the Standard Model as a quantum error-correcting code
abstract: Together with a right-handed neutrino, the fermions of one generation of the Standard Model are labelled by five bits, a combinatorial structure tied to anomaly cancellation. We make this precise. Anomaly cancellation is the vanishing of a cubic form, the defining property of triorthogonal codes, the quantum error-correcting codes behind magic state distillation. Removing the right-handed neutrino gives a $[[15,1,3]]_p$ code for every prime $p$, including the Bravyi-Kitaev code for $p = 2$. For qutrits it is the unique shortest distance-three triorthogonal code.
summary: This work demonstrates that the fermion content of one Standard Model generation forms a quantum error-correcting code due to the mathematical constraint of anomaly cancellation. This code is identified as a specific triorthogonal $[[15, 1, 3]]_p$ code. The paper bridges particle physics (SO(10) GUTs) and quantum information theory by showing that fundamental symmetries dictate robust quantum encoding structures.
main_problem: The paper establishes a deep connection between the anomaly cancellation conditions in the Standard Model and the mathematical structure required for a quantum error-correcting code.
main_result: The fermions of one Standard Model generation, when combined with a right-handed neutrino, form a triorthogonal quantum error-correcting code, specifically a $[[15, 1, 3]]_p$ code.
method: The authors use lattice theory and the mathematical requirement of vanishing cubic anomalies (a defining property of triorthogonal codes) to prove the code structure.
model_or_system: The system is the Standard Model fermions embedded within an SO(10) grand unification framework. The code is constructed using the charge structure of these fermions, treating them as qudits.
key_observables: Code parameters like length ($n=15$), distance ($d=3$), and the existence of logical operators derived from anomaly cancellation.
important_parameters: The prime modulus $p$ (especially $p=2$ and $p \ge 5$), and the structure of the SO(10) symmetry group.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the $SO(10)$ embedding and the assumption that anomaly cancellation dictates the code structure. Special care is taken for $p=2$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the fifteen-qudit code as a doubled structure, linking the right-handed fields and the logical qudit. Tables summarize code structure, stabilizers, and distillation performance.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the mathematical equivalence between anomaly cancellation and triorthogonal codes. It then constructs the code using the Standard Model charges, deriving the $[[15, 1, 3]]_p$ parameters. Finally, it analyzes the code's properties, including its relationship to other known codes and its performance in quantum state distillation.
why_interesting: The paper provides a concrete, physical realization of a highly structured quantum code using fundamental particle physics symmetries, linking high-energy theory directly to quantum information theory.
